02Science & Brand

Making NAD+ a household name

Take longevity science from the research lab to a brand people know and trust.

RoleVice President of Creative

ExpertiseCreative Direction, Content, Performance

Era2016–2020, 2025–Present

When I joined Elysium, longevity science was still fringe and NAD+ mostly lived in research labs. Later in my tenure, The Wall Street Journal was calling Elysium’s chief scientist the “grandfather of the booming longevity movement.” As one of the company’s first creative hires, I helped translate complex science into a brand people could understand, trust, and care about.

From my experience in magazines and as an Ironman triathlete, I knew longevity was going to eat wellness’s lunch. I went straight to the source: NAD+ conferences, Harvard and MIT labs, and became a category expert in the research itself. That became Endpoints, a science and culture publication that published 100 stories, grew to 30,000 Medium followers, and reached 65,000+ monthly readers—all in under two years. I launched The Abstract, now one of longevity’s longest-running newsletters and a major revenue driver. Our work ranked at the top of Google and was republished by universities and research labs.

After taking time to pursue my own projects and build a life in Colorado, Elysium asked me back as Vice President of Creative. I restructured the team, built a new visual identity and brand language system, developed an advertising engine, adapted workflows in the AI boom, and led creative for launches including Creatine+, The Elysium Longevity Institute, and more.
